summary: Under section 319 of the Crimes Act 1958, a person who drives dangerously and causes death is liable to a maximum of 10 years imprisonment (level 5).

Under section 71 of the Drugs, Poisons and Controlled Substances Act 1981, trafficking a large commercial quantity of a drug of dependence is an indictable offence with a maximum penalty of level 2 imprisonment (25 years).

Under section 37 of the Sentencing Act 1991, a community correction order is a sentencing order that allows an offender to serve their sentence in the community subject to conditions, instead of imprisonment.

Under section 22 of the Infringements Act 2006, a person can apply in writing to the enforcement agency that issued the infringement notice for an internal review, setting out the grounds for the review.
Under section 1 of the Road Safety Act 1986, the Act's purposes include providing for safe, efficient and equitable road use and setting out the general obligations of road users.
Under section 1 of the Victoria Police Act 2013, the Act's purposes are to re-enact and modernise the law governing Victoria Police and to replace the Police Regulation Act 1958.

Driving dangerously and causing serious injury is an offence under section 319 of the Crimes Act 1958. If alcohol was involved, section 49 of the Road Safety Act 1986 (offences involving alcohol or other drugs) may also apply, potentially alongside the Crimes Act offence.

Under section 43 of the Sentencing Act 1991, a court may impose both a fine and a community correction order (as defined in section 37) for the same offence, since the Act allows combining certain sentencing orders.

Under section 22 of the Infringements Act 2006, a person may apply for an internal review of an infringement notice, but under section 27, that review is terminated if the matter instead proceeds to court.

Yes — section 71AB of the Drugs, Poisons and Controlled Substances Act 1981 specifically criminalises trafficking a drug of dependence to a child, which is treated as a distinct and more serious offence than the general trafficking offence in section 71AC.
Under section 50AAA of the Road Safety Act 1986, a driver can be directed to have an alcohol interlock condition imposed. Section 50AAC sets out the driver's right to appeal against that condition.

Section 200J of the Victoria Police Act 2013 authorises members of Victoria Police to use reasonable force, and section 10 clarifies who else, beyond police officers themselves, counts as a member of the force for the purposes of the Act.
